title: Red Sea water temperature by month 2026
body_markdown:
The Red Sea off Hurghada runs from **21°C (70°F) in February**, the coldest month, up to **30°C (86°F) in August**, the warmest — a swing of 9°C across the year that decides what you wear in the water and which trip you book.


**TL;DR**

- Red sea water temperature by month in 2026 ranges from 21°C (70°F) in February to 30°C (86°F) in August.
- The annual average sits near 26°C (79°F), warm enough for snorkeling without a wetsuit from June through October.
- December through March is the only stretch where a 3-5mm wetsuit makes a real difference on longer dives.
- August and September are the warmest months but also the busiest for boat trips out of Hurghada.




## Why this matters

Water temperature is the single biggest variable in how a Red Sea trip actually feels. A diver in a shorty wetsuit in February is cold within 30 minutes; the same diver in August barely needs neoprene at all.

Anyone planning [Hurghada snorkeling and diving trips](https://dailyredsea.com/) around a specific month should check this table before booking gear or a boat slot — not after landing at the resort and realizing the water is colder than the beach felt.

## Red sea water temperature by month

The table below tracks average sea-surface temperature for the Hurghada coast across the year, based on multi-year averaged sea-surface data for the Red Sea. Depth, wind, and distance from shore shift the number a degree or two either way — reef walls at 20 meters run cooler than the shallows where most snorkeling happens.

| Month | Avg water temp (°C) | Avg water temp (°F) | Wetsuit guidance |
|---|---|---|---|
| January | 22°C | 72°F | 3-5mm recommended |
| February | 21°C | 70°F | 3-5mm recommended |
| March | 22°C | 72°F | 3mm useful |
| April | 24°C | 75°F | 3mm or shorty |
| May | 26°C | 79°F | Shorty or rash guard |
| June | 28°C | 82°F | Rash guard, no wetsuit needed |
| July | 29°C | 84°F | Rash guard, no wetsuit needed |
| August | 30°C | 86°F | Rash guard, no wetsuit needed |
| September | 29°C | 84°F | Rash guard, no wetsuit needed |
| October | 28°C | 82°F | Rash guard, no wetsuit needed |
| November | 26°C | 79°F | Shorty or rash guard |
| December | 24°C | 75°F | 3mm or shorty |
| **Annual average** | **26°C** | **79°F** | Reference row for the whole year |

**August leads the year at 30°C (86°F); February trails at 21°C (70°F)** — an 9-degree Celsius spread between the two ends of the calendar. May through October all sit at or above 26°C (79°F), which is the point where most divers stop needing exposure protection beyond a rash guard.

Methodology: figures reflect averaged sea-surface temperature readings for the Hurghada coastal zone across multiple years, rounded to the nearest whole degree. One limitation worth naming directly — surface readings near a beach run warmer than open water a kilometer out, and a reef wall at depth can run 1-2°C cooler than the number in this table.

## How to use these benchmarks

- **Booking a winter trip (December-March):** budget for a 3-5mm wetsuit on any dive longer than 30 minutes; snorkeling still works fine in a rash guard for shorter sessions.
- **Booking peak summer (July-September):** water sits at 28-30°C (82-86°F) — comfortable enough that many snorkelers skip exposure gear entirely, but this is also when [best snorkeling trips in Hurghada](https://dailyredsea.byryze.com/best-snorkeling-trips-in-hurghada-for-first-time-visitors) get booked out fastest.
- **Shoulder months (April, May, October, November):** the 24-26°C (75-79°F) range is the sweet spot most divers rate as most comfortable — warm enough for long sessions, cool enough to avoid the August crowds.
- **New or nervous swimmers:** pick a month where the table shows 26°C (79°F) or higher; colder water makes snorkeling feel more physically demanding, which matters more for a first-timer than an experienced diver.


![Snorkeler over a shallow Red Sea coral reef in warm clear water](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/438acfcc-7e4a-4ca7-94ef-ec4c7ed03c57/body-9ac10a4321e485ae54a11b894e344417.jpg)

*Warm-season months are when most first-time snorkelers skip a wetsuit altogether.*


Divers planning a longer stay should also [prepare for scuba diving in Hurghada](https://dailyredsea.byryze.com/how-to-prepare-for-scuba-diving-in-hurghada) with the right exposure gear for whichever month they land in — the same trip in February and August calls for a different kit bag.

## Water temperature and the diving calendar

Temperature is only half the planning picture. Visibility, wind, and crowd levels shift on a different schedule than temperature does, which is why the warmest month isn't automatically the best month.

- **June-August:** warmest water (28-30°C / 82-86°F), busiest boats, higher demand for [off-season excursion deals in Hurghada](https://dailyredsea.com/blog/off-season-excursion-deals-in-hurghada-for-summer-travelers) as operators try to fill slower midweek slots.
- **September-November:** water still holds at 26-29°C (79-84°F) with fewer crowds — often the best value window of the year.
- **December-February:** coldest water (21-24°C / 70-75°F), calmer seas most days, and the season when [liveaboard diving trips from Hurghada](https://dailyredsea.byryze.com/best-liveaboard-diving-trips-from-hurghada) run some of their clearest visibility of the year despite the cooler temperature.

**Verdict: for comfort without a wetsuit, May through October is the window; for the clearest, quietest water, accept the cold and dive December through February in a 5mm suit.**

## FAQ


**What is the average Red Sea water temperature by month?**

It ranges from 21°C (70°F) in February to 30°C (86°F) in August, with an annual average near 26°C (79°F) across the Hurghada coast.

**What is the coldest month for Red Sea water temperature?**

February is the coldest month at roughly 21°C (70°F). January and March run close behind at 22°C (72°F).

**What is the warmest month to swim in the Red Sea?**

August is the warmest month at around 30°C (86°F), with July and September close behind at 29°C (84°F).

**Do you need a wetsuit to snorkel in the Red Sea in 2026?**

From June through October, water runs 28-30°C (82-86°F) and most snorkelers skip a wetsuit entirely. December through March, a 3-5mm wetsuit makes longer sessions far more comfortable.

**Is the Red Sea warm enough to dive year-round?**

Yes. Even the coldest month, February, averages 21°C (70°F), which is diveable in a 5mm wetsuit. Nothing in the calendar drops the water below comfortable diving range.

**When is Red Sea water the most comfortable for beginners?**

April, May, October, and November sit in the 24-26°C (75-79°F) range, warm enough for long sessions without the peak-summer crowds of July and August.

**Does Red Sea water temperature affect visibility?**

Not directly, but the two shift on different calendars — the coolest months (December-February) often bring some of the clearest visibility of the year despite the lower temperature.

**How much colder is the water at depth compared to the surface?**

Reef walls and deeper dive sites typically run 1-2°C cooler than the surface readings in the table above, which matters most on dives past 15-20 meters.


## One last thing

The biggest planning mistake isn't picking a cold month — it's assuming August's 30°C (86°F) water means an easier trip. Peak warmth lines up with peak demand, so the same warm water that lets you skip a wetsuit also means booking further ahead for a boat slot.
